topic: The Pi-Collision Mystery: From Bouncing Blocks to Digits of π

sections.title: The Setup: The Elastic Collision Paradox
lecture_lines: Two blocks move on a frictionless surface.
A small block approaches a stationary large block.
A wall sits behind the large block.
animations: Display two blocks, small (left) and large (right), on a horizontal #FFFFFF line.
Small block moves right towards the large block.
Show a vertical #FFFFFF line behind the large block as a wall.

sections.title: The Pattern: Counting the Collisions
lecture_lines: Collisions occur between the blocks and wall.
The count depends on the mass ratio.
animations: Show small block colliding with large block, then large with wall.
Vary mass ratio between blocks visually by scaling the block sizes.
Animate 31 collision cycles for a 100x mass ratio.

sections.title: The Bridge: Geometry in Motion
lecture_lines: Map block motion to circular geometry.
The angle relates to the mass ratio.
Collision count approximates the arc length.
Visualize the movement on a circle.
animations: Project block positions onto a unit circle as angles.
Show angle increment proportional to the square root of mass ratio.
Draw arc segments on the circle for each collision.
Highlight the mapping between physics and geometric arcs.
Display rotating vector to visualize motion around the circle.

sections.title: The Revelation: Calculating Pi
lecture_lines: Mass ratios reveal digits of pi.
Each digit emerges from the collisions.
animations: Show the mass ratio 100, 10000, 1000000 displaying digits 3, 1, 4.
Highlight the decimal digits appearing as collisions conclude.
Display the formula for collision count approximating pi.
Connect specific digit sequences to final block velocities.
Demonstrate the mechanical process yielding digits of pi.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Beauty of Abstraction
animations: Overlay physics collision data with abstract circle geometry.
Transition collision animation into a static mathematical constant.
Fade out blocks to leave a glowing pi symbol on screen.
